content_of_post_to_comment: A paradox: Minimally guided instruction sees creativity, curiosity and critical thinking as inputs, ie general skills to be cultivated directly and then sort of aimed at content. In contrast, explicit instruction treats them as outputs, ie the by-product of deep, well-organised domain knowledge, not things you can train in the abstract. In other words, progressive education sees creativity/curiosity/critical thinking as things you need to teach explicitly ("we need to teach 21st Century skills not facts" etc) whereas explicit instruction sees these things as emerging naturally, or as a by-product of having learned a lot of knowledge about a domain.
